answer: To resist Sybil attacks, the protocol imposes cryptographic stake burning on every identity registration. Rather than static collateral, each delta identity registered under a cluster incurs a superlinear cost scaling as $C(n) = k \cdot n^{1.8}$. Validating nodes mirror network states to verify that burned tokens match this superlinear curve, creating an economic dune over which coordinated multi-agent fraud faces insurmountable quadratic friction.
